Replay

Typed authored archetypes

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

For scripted actors, Script_Archetypes owns callback configuration and retains appearance resources. Its source registry can close after initialization. Use the lower-level APIs below when custom bindings need explicit control of the borrowed registry and callback lifetimes.

Use a stable gameplay ID to connect a value definition to local scene assets:

Odin
assets: scenegd.Archetype_Assets(Enemy_Definition)
scenegd.archetype_assets_init(&assets, MAX_ENEMY_KINDS)
entries := []defs.Archetype(Enemy_Definition, scenegd.Archetype_Visual){
    {id=6, definition=storm_definition, local={storm_scene, storm_style}},
}
report := scenegd.archetype_assets_publish(&assets, entries, []u32{6})

definitions.Registry(Definition, Local) is engine-independent. Definition must be a replayable value; Local may borrow pointers. IDs include zero and are bounded by the explicit ID limit (maximum 65,536). Publication rejects duplicates, missing required IDs, out-of-range IDs and typed validator failures before swapping the complete registry. Lookup is direct by ID. Reports retain their diagnostic text. The pure registry owns arrays, not objects referenced by Local.

Archetype_Assets adds Godot ownership: each entry must have a PackedScene and may have an appearance Resource. Publication retains every accepted resource before releasing the prior set. Failed publication preserves the prior set. Candidates must stay alive until publication finishes. Game-specific Resource script/range checks belong in the extractor before calling this API.

Archetype_Pool2(Entity, Display, Rig) combines those registrations with typed scene bindings. Initialize it with an immutable asset registry, a capacity, a select(Display)->u32 callback, and a binding factory receiving the ID, copied definition and local assets. Present ordinary View_Item batches through archetype_pool_present. It rejects unknown IDs and duplicate entity identities across archetypes before changing view lifetimes. Different IDs may use different PackedScenes and scene compositions with the same typed display interface.

Each registered scene has a View_Pool2. The archetype pool partitions input items into fixed scratch buffers, with no partition-buffer allocation during steady presentation. Creating scenes runs their normal Godot lifecycle and can fail. Preflight validates input before scene changes, but it cannot roll back arbitrary work performed by user _ready procedures.

Keep the parent and asset owner alive until all dependent views have been destroyed. Destroy/recreate the pools before replacing the asset registry. Keep callback configuration at stable addresses. Views may borrow appearance scripts only for that lifetime. Resource pointers never enter Display, World, input or checkpoints.

Memory use grows with the configured ID limit and capacity per archetype, even when few nodes are active. The partition bound is 1,048,576 item slots; each individual capacity is also bounded by view.MAX_INDEX_CAPACITY. During a kind change or scope reset, retired Godot nodes may await deferred deletion, as in the underlying view pool. Applications with very large catalogs may prefer their own shared-capacity scene pool or a specialized renderer. This convenience layer is optional.

Scrapyard stores one ScrapEnemyArchetype Resource in archetypes/enemies per enemy. It references a MobDef (whose ID is the wire identity), a PackedScene and a ScrapEnemyStyle. The loader validates definitions, required IDs and exact style scripts, publishes the complete set, then binds the scene's one appearance input. The enemy scene has no per-kind Resource slots or fixed skin array. Its standalone preview exports one appearance so it remains editable without a game/session.
